# Implementation status and acceptance boundaries

This stable path is the current status index, not a chronological TODO list or a
claim that every topology/platform combination has been verified. Feature and
protocol details belong to the linked owning guides; Git history records completed
work.

## Current capability areas

| Area                       | Implemented behavior                                                                                                                             | Reference / boundary                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Direct conversations       | Signed discovery, identity-pinned Noise/TCP, encrypted account-addressed DMs, replies, reactions, mentions, search and retained history.         | [Architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); discovery and TCP reachability remain separate.                                                                                                |
| Groups                     | Signed membership controls, sender-key encryption, bounded fanout and authorized member recovery with per-member sharing.                        | [Group flows and scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery); a removed/nonmember device cannot acquire authority from discovery. |
| Relay networking           | Equal trusted post offices, shared public enrollment, opaque custody/federation, direct-first attempts, soft preference and alternatives.        | [Network baseline](../docs/network-design-reference.md); an alternate needs a surviving onward route.                                                                                   |
| Network controls           | Per-device master/send/receive/directory preferences, physical-LAN-only discovery and direct LAN/Tailscale relay selection.                      | [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md); visibility does not grant conversation authority or create a firewall.                                                                 |
| Files and folders          | Encrypted chunks, exact-offer consent, durable decisions, restart recovery, integrity checks and recipient completion.                           | [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion); card arrival is not byte completion.                                                           |
| Linked devices             | Code-authorized enrollment, certified sibling synchronization and device-local category preferences.                                             | [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization); full replay needs its own live authenticated route.                            |
| Calls                      | Optional device-addressed live Noise signaling and separate WebRTC media.                                                                        | No post-office signaling fallback or TURN service; native WebView and physical capture acceptance remain separate.                                                                      |
| Desktop presentation       | Shared person/relay classification, account/device profile details, themes, avatars, stickers, virtualized navigation and optional pack installation. | [Visual system](../frontend/DESIGN.md) · [Customization packs](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).                                                                                         |
| Local privacy and recovery | Privacy presets, lock controls, hidden contacts, local retention, recall and encrypted manual backup/restore.                                    | [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) · [Backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md); restore creates a new device and cannot revoke an old one.                                      |

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.
# Performance requirements

Read this before changing background work, synchronization, storage, caches or UI
state. Mesh Talk should cost little while waiting, load data when needed and stay
bounded as history grows. This guide owns cross-cutting performance requirements;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md), [network budgets](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and [reliability rules](ai-coding-reliability.md) own their implementation contracts.

## Budgets and measurement

These are initial project targets, **not industry standards or claims that the
current application meets them**. Establish a production-build baseline on each
supported platform. Reference fixture: 4 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, 100 contacts,
20 groups and 100,000 stored messages; no pending transfers, calls or animations.
Separate cold start, warm start, catch-up, visible idle and hidden idle. Measure a
quiet five-minute window after warmup; record build, runtime, profile and workload.
Warm startup restarts the process with OS caches retained; cold startup records
its uncached/first-launch conditions. Usable means an actionable list or
conversation, not a blank shell; report human authorization waits separately.
The empty-shell comparison keeps the same backend, runtime, process membership
and window settings, with user payloads absent.

| Resource                | Initial target for the reference fixture                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Idle CPU                | Visible desktop: ≤1% of one logical CPU; hidden desktop: ≤0.25%; headless node: ≤0.5%, averaged over the window.                                                                                    |
| Retained memory         | Headless node: ≤64 MiB private commit. Desktop: ≤64 MiB workload delta above the same-build empty shell; establish a reviewed whole-family ceiling from that baseline.                              |
| Memory growth           | Repeated navigation/media cycles reach a bounded plateau. Tenfold stored history must not require tenfold startup reads or retained UI payloads.                                                    |
| Idle writes             | Zero busin…334 tokens truncated…acts, not this guide.

An existing target miss requires recorded baseline and an owned follow-up; it is
not permission to worsen the path or silently raise its budget. A target change
requires comparable evidence and review. Migrations, catch-up and active media have
separate bounded work budgets and progress evidence, not an unlimited exception.

## Apply to every feature

Before implementation, identify the owning producer, its meaningful trigger,
bounded work unit, retained resources and stop condition. Review all three phases,
including costs introduced in another process or on another device:

| Phase           | Required design and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Startup         | Load indexed summaries and the active conversation's bounded page first. Defer inactive history, attachment bytes and optional features until demanded. Avoid decrypting all history, rebuilding unchanged indexes or republishing unchanged state at each login. Measure time to usable UI, peak memory, bytes read and writes separately from catch-up; migrations need resumable bounded progress.                    |
| Idle            | With unchanged inputs, settle business producers and avoid business-data writes. Use scoped events and exact next deadlines; coalesce noncritical repair into the existing serial queue, normally at least five minutes apart. A heartbeat, read, empty reply or offline device must not restart historical work. Verify visible and hidden states, including renderer/helpers and remote work triggered by this client. |
| Active business | Bound each query, decrypt, decode, transfer and rendering turn by items and bytes. Drain real available work promptly with backpressure and cancellation; user interaction and reception must remain responsive. Measure latency, peak CPU/memory and I/O for send/receive, catch-up, search, media and navigation as applicable, then prove resources settle when work finishes.                                        |

Do not classify a permanently retrying historical queue as an unlimited active
workload. Distinguish actionable progress from blocked work, record its outcome
and retain a bounded retry deadline. Successful reads, metadata comparisons and
already-held custody are not new user data. Serializing unnecessary work or
lengthening a timer alone does not establish that its cost is justified.

For every affected phase, the PR must state the trigger and stop condition,
resource bound, selected regression and measured result or explicit evidence gap.
Exercise unchanged inputs, growing history, unavailable dependencies and owner
replacement where applicable. Compare the same workload before and after; verify
return to idle and memory reclamation after repeated use. Do not infer low power
from a quiet disk, fast startup from a blank window, or bounded memory from one
snapshot. Existing misses remain explicit follow-ups with an owning module and
reproduction; never describe a passing correctness test as performance acceptance.

## Design and review rules

1. **Trigger work from meaning.** Prefer committed changes, scoped invalidations,
   user navigation and foreground activation. Schedule the next actual expiry or
   retry deadline. Empty success is not progress and must not keep a fast retry
   hot. Coalesce duplicate wakes; retain bounded dirty work while a task is busy.
   Pending work still owns its retry deadline. Suppress unchanged ordinary wakes
   using scheduling evidence, independently of successful completion; preserve
   explicit drivers and event-only progress when no timer owns continuation.
   A retained blocked task is not evidence of progress: keep its recovery fact
   while backing off, and resume promptly on dependency changes. Local pagination
   and actual received bytes retain prompt continuation.
   Reconfirming an already-held relay copy is not new progress. Park unchanged
   successful reconciliation until sparse repair; keep authenticated recipient
   delivery and actual custody-loss recovery separate from that scheduling hint.
   A bounded historical scan must also become quiet after its complete sweep;
   preserve prompt unfinished pages and separate lightweight claim rechecks.
   Qualify scan completion against current source and semantic inputs, before
   and after work. Failed discovery keeps a separate bounded wait; it cannot
   acknowledge EOF or repeatedly hydrate the same blocked item on observer wakes.
   Preserve invalidation domains through batching and acknowledgement; a roster
   heartbeat must not reload unrelated settings or history. Empty pages do not
   imply a global change. Presentation metadata does not renew user activity.
## Validation stages and agent responsibilities

Validation depth and business capability are separate dimensions. Use the same
owning contracts at each depth; a development result never promotes itself into
candidate acceptance. This follows staged pipelines and actionable feedback as
described by [Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/DeploymentPipeline.html) and
[Software Engineering at Google](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch23.html).

| Stage                | Trigger and purpose                                                                          | Entry or evidence                                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Understand and plan  | Start work or change its scope; identify business owner, consumers and obligations           | Owning guides, `make verify-plan`                                                    |
| Change feedback      | Validate a small change with affected static checks and executable tests                     | `make verify-changed`, development feedback JSON                                     |
| Boundary validation  | Change cross-module interfaces, runtime IPC, visible behavior, persistence or lifecycle      | Plan requirements and escalation review; focused integration/browser/native evidence |
| Candidate acceptance | Accept the current committed PR head before merge                                            | Required protected CI; optional local `prepare-pr.sh` and full health                |
| Extended validation  | Scheduled, release or explicitly triggered compatibility, stress and long-running properties | Owning backend/UI/native workflows and evaluation guides                             |

Read the selected capability's authoritative guide before changing behavior.
Declare semantic risks that source imports cannot express, inspect automatic
consumers and boundary requirements, and add missing owners/scenarios with a
reason. AI may expand scope; it cannot remove mandatory selections because it
judges a change low risk. Preserve the distinction between local acceptance,
recipient delivery and read state, and between frontend ownership and host
session authority. Summarize observed results and remaining obligations before
moving to candidate acceptance.

section='''## Current-IM foundation inventory

This bounded F01 map routes the eight [foundation scenarios](development-roadmap.md#required-scenario-inventory)
to existing owners. It supplements the detailed feature map below; it does not
replace the glossary or certify runtime behavior. **Implemented** means a current
source path was inspected; **partial** means only a narrower boundary is covered;
**unknown** means evidence must still be collected. No new missing product
capability or confirmed defect was established by this inspection. Future SDK,
forum, PWA and replacement UI work remain deferred by the roadmap.

### Concepts, authority and existing consumers

Paths use `core/` for `crates/mesh-talk-core/src/` and `ui/` for
`frontend/src/`. Domain definitions remain in [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md).

| Boundary | Existing producer and consumer | Invariant and inspection status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local user, account and device | Desktop `runtime_bootstrap.rs::spawn_node_runtime` consumes a `SessionLease` and starts core `NodeRuntime`; `identity/` and `node/account_devices.rs` own cryptographic identity. | Implemented: the host data-directory account identifier is explicitly distinct from the cryptographic account. Names and addresses cannot establish device authority. |
| Desktop session, participant, transport and ratchet | `src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs` fences host operations; `core/node/participant_runtime.rs` owns producers; `core/node/session_pool.rs` and `core/ratchet/` own different protocol lifetimes. `ui/store/ownership.ts` fences presentation completions. | Implemented seams; UI cancellation explicitly does not abort an admitted native operation. Complete native retirement remains unknown. |
| Conversation, member and pending operation | `src-tauri/src/chat_commands/channels.rs` adapts channel sends; `core/node/channels.rs` accepts then flushes them. `node/account_group/` owns account operation/access state; `channel_account_authority.rs` owns signed membership. | Keep pending operations distinct from effective public events and announcements distinct from membership grants. The [account ownership contract](#account-and-device-ownership) remains authoritative; full transition qualification is F04 work. |
| Acceptance, custody, delivery and read | Typed `ui/lib/api/chat.ts` calls desktop messaging adapters; `core/node/outgoing_message.rs` supplies retry-safe integration acceptance; `delivery_store.rs`, `delivery_runtime.rs`, `delivery_receipt.rs` and account read documents retain separate outcomes. | Implemented: request-ID reuse checks content digest and rechecks host authorization. Acceptance is not recipient delivery or reading. Ordinary sends and integration requests have distinct entry points. |
| Removal, recall and cleanup | `core/node/account_documents/personal.rs` represents Delete, Reopen and Applied controls; sibling history import consumes their permission cut. `node/recall.rs` owns a different operation. | Implemented: hidden state, history clearing, deletion floor and local cleanup completion are distinct. No global deletion or safe marker reclamation claim. |
| Disclosure and local integration access | `core/node/privacy_routes.rs` provides historical route hints; authenticated transport verifies identity. `src-tauri/src/integrations.rs` adapts the integration service; MCP is a separate transport adapter. | Route hints are not proof. Grant expiry, destination rights and exact-session authority must be checked at acceptance, not inferred from a UI state or discovery result. See [integration contracts](bot-integrations.md). |

### Stores and resource ownership

Retain the existing [storage architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[performance requirements](performance-requirements.md); this map proposes no
migration or new cache. Storage format presence is not a performance diagnosis.

| Category | Current owner and real consumer | Resource/recovery boundary and next evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profile identity and encrypted indexed data | `core/storage/profile/`, `storage/database.rs`; event repository and transcript repository consume the profile connection. | SQLCipher owns connection/cache/WAL settings. Production and test KDF settings differ; F03 must record resolved build features before startup measurements. Per-connection cache limits are not process memory limits. |
| Signed events and transcript projections | `core/eventlog/repository/`, `eventlog/persist.rs`, `node/transcript_repository/`; history, sync and search consume them. | Transcript headers and bodies are separate; page admission bounds rows and bytes. Legacy import code remains in `eventlog/persist/legacy.rs`; it is not evidence that every current query uses legacy storage. F03 measures metadata scans separately from decoded payloads. |
| Durable outgoing state | `core/node/delivery_store.rs` consumes encrypted record logs for journal and outbox; delivery runtime and receipts consume transitions. | Coexists with indexed storage. F04 must qualify interrupted acceptance/reopen and sender-state recovery before any extraction or compaction. |
| Personal controls and replay evidence | `core/node/account_documents/personal.rs`, `account_sync/`; account-history import consumes deletion floors and source cuts. | Keep replay suppression until its owning contract permits reclamation. F04 qualifies restart/restore and genuinely new content separately. |
| File cards, bytes and completion | `core/node/files.rs`, `file_consent.rs`, `file_completion.rs`, `group_file_delivery.rs`; desktop `chat_commands/files.rs` and attachment UI consume them. | Card visibility, exact-offer consent, verified chunks and completion are separate. Replica budget is not an overall attachment quota; F03 measures temporary/output files and repeated media use. |
| UI state and transient projections | `ui/store/chat.ts`, `ownership.ts`, conversation components; host events and typed API results are inputs. | Generation checks prevent stale publication but do not establish backend cancellation. F03 includes renderer/helper processes, repeated navigation and return to idle. |

### Scenario routes and available verification

Entries below identify reusable evidence inputs, **not fresh passing runs**.
Use each crate's `validation.json`, `frontend/validation.json` and the
[validation planner](testing-feedback-loop.md#change-aware-development-plans)
to select actual commands for a changed boundary. A test filename alone does not
establish its assertions, source selection or platform coverage.

| Required scenario | Existing owner/caller route | Representative evidence input and remaining limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup/unlock with retained history | Desktop runtime bootstrap → `NodeRuntime` → profile storage and participant preparation. | `core-startup-identity` and `core-indexed-current-profiles` capability contracts; participant preparation tests. F03 still needs production cold/warm time-to-usable UI, retained-data scale and interrupted initialization evidence. |
| Visible/hidden idle | Participant event/deadline waits → file/recovery producers; chat store → conversation viewport. | Inspected `participant_runtime_tests.rs` scheduling paths and `ConversationViewIdle.test.ts`: the latter changes peer-check timestamps without viewport rerenders and retains new-message behavior. Mocked rendering does not measure native CPU, wakeups or hidden-window reception. |
| Direct/group messaging | `ui/lib/api/chat.ts` → desktop `messaging.rs` / `channels.rs` → core DM/channel acceptance → delivery. | `delivery_store_tests.rs`, `delivery_runtime_tests.rs`, `delivery_receipt_tests.rs` and `core-account-group-operations` are existing selectors to audit in F02. Full assertion coverage, recipient scales and return-to-idle timings remain unqualified here. |
| Linked-device/group catch-up | Certified sibling `account_sync/` and group custody/session paths consume separate authority. | `account_sync/selection_tests.rs`, `personal_replay_tests.rs` and `core-shared-channel-custody`. F04 must qualify duplicate/reordered/interrupted pages and revoked membership; loopback evidence cannot certify physical topology. |
| History/search/navigation | Host owner-scoped search → `core/node/search.rs` / transcript repository → UI results. | Inspected `recent_search_reports_recent_window_and_does_not_find_older_match`: excludes a match outside the 2,000-entry window. Search metadata scans and bounded payload decoding are distinct costs. `core-search-references` owns selectors; F03 measures repeated navigation/cache growth. |
| Attachments/media | Attachment intake → desktop files adapter → consent/chunks/completion → UI media. | `core-file`, `core-file-consent-tests`, `core-file-message-identity`, `core-group-file-relay`; existing source coverage is partial evidence only. F02 audits cancellation, corrupt/incomplete source and retry assertions; F03 needs native decode and cleanup measurements. |
| Delete/restart/restore | Personal controls → cleanup acknowledgements → sibling history admission; backup/restore is a separate host route. | Inspected `buffered_archive_page_cannot_acquire_permission_from_a_later_cleanup_ack`: old buffered content stays absent, unrelated content imports, a fresh authorized request can add new content. This does not qualify full backup restoration or all marker lifetimes. |
| Lock/logout/sleep/owner replacement | Desktop session admission → participant stop; frontend generation fences publication. | Inspected `stop_waits_for_owned_blocking_work_after_host_cancellation`: stop waits for a held worker, joins after release and rejects later work. Native sleep/resume, all host producers and exact-session integration retirement still require composition evidence. |

### Downstream handoffs and finite unknowns

The integration owner accepts these inputs through the roadmap's review gates.
Until then they are a proposed static map. F05–F08 do not gain construction
permission from an inventory or from the existence of a test.

| Handoff / decision owner | Falsifiable next action | Admission/stop condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F02 — validation owner | For the eight rows, resolve capability selectors, inspect actual assertions and collect one source-bound focused attempt with setup/compile/execution/retry timings. Audit existing `scripts/validation/{affected,checks,feedback,latency}.mjs` and CI ownership before adding tooling. | Produce an assertion-gap and check-allocation proposal; preserve required checks. Broader REQ-003/030 method classification stays explicitly outstanding. No full-suite run is needed for this static map. |
| F03 — runtime/performance owner | Establish production build/features, OS/architecture, process family and fixture identity; measure startup, five-minute settled visible/hidden idle, one messaging/catch-up workload and return to idle using existing budgets. | No inference from fast-test KDF or synthetic test timing to shipped performance. If provenance or quiet measurement conditions are unavailable, record the exact missing input and stop performance conclusions. |
| F04 — core authority and desktop lifecycle owners | Trace the selected send/delete operation through host admission, durable commit, replay/restart and owner replacement; qualify public membership, private removal and announcement authority separately. | Resolve the needed contract with failure/recovery evidence. Product-policy ambiguity goes to the product owner; inspection uncertainty is not a confirmed defect. |
| F05/F06 — module and scheduling owners | Reuse participant preparation/launch/stop, runtime admission and meaningful event/deadline waits unless an accepted baseline demonstrates a concrete gap. | No universal scheduler or file-count-driven extraction. Require a real consumer and accepted F02/F03/F04 inputs. |
| F07/F08 — communication and storage owners | Use separate personal/group replay authority and separate indexed/log/file resource categories when ranking a measured slice. | No storage replacement, deletion-floor reclamation or protocol change without compatibility/recovery evidence. |
| F09/F10 — validation and integration owners | Bind each admitted slice to its existing contract/selector, then assemble the eight scenario results with source/platform limitations. | Static documentation does not satisfy integrated acceptance; future features remain deferred. |

No current code/contract contradiction was confirmed in this bounded inspection.
The unresolved items above are evidence gaps, not claims that the entire
implementation is correct or that each named test covers its whole subsystem.

'''
s=s.replace('## 1. Dependency direction',section+'## 1. Dependency direction',1)
p.write_text(s)

+## Current-IM foundation inventory
+
+This bounded F01 map routes the eight [foundation scenarios](development-roadmap.md#required-scenario-inventory)
+to existing owners. It supplements the detailed feature map below; it does not
+replace the glossary or certify runtime behavior. **Implemented** means a current
+source path was inspected; **partial** means only a narrower boundary is covered;
+**unknown** means evidence must still be collected. No new missing product
+capability or confirmed defect was established by this inspection. Future SDK,
+forum, PWA and replacement UI work remain deferred by the roadmap.
+
+### Concepts, authority and existing consumers
+
+Paths use `core/` for `crates/mesh-talk-core/src/` and `ui/` for
+`frontend/src/`. Domain definitions remain in [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md).
+
+| Boundary | Existing producer and consumer | Invariant and inspection status |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Local user, account and device | Desktop `runtime_bootstrap.rs::spawn_node_runtime` consumes a `SessionLease` and starts core `NodeRuntime`; `identity/` and `node/account_devices.rs` own cryptographic identity. | Implemented: the host data-directory account identifier is explicitly distinct from the cryptographic account. Names and addresses cannot establish device authority. |
+| Desktop session, participant, transport and ratchet | `src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs` fences host operations; `core/node/participant_runtime.rs` owns producers; `core/node/session_pool.rs` and `core/ratchet/` own different protocol lifetimes. `ui/store/ownership.ts` fences presentation completions. | Implemented seams; UI cancellation explicitly does not abort an admitted native operation. Complete native retirement remains unknown. |
+| Conversation, member and pending operation | `src-tauri/src/chat_commands/channels.rs` adapts channel sends; `core/node/channels.rs` accepts then flushes them. `node/account_group/` owns account operation/access state; `channel_account_authority.rs` owns signed membership. | Keep pending operations distinct from effective public events and announcements distinct from membership grants. The [account ownership contract](#account-and-device-ownership) remains authoritative; full transition qualification is F04 work. |
+| Acceptance, custody, delivery and read | Typed `ui/lib/api/chat.ts` calls desktop messaging adapters; `core/node/outgoing_message.rs` supplies retry-safe integration acceptance; `delivery_store.rs`, `delivery_runtime.rs`, `delivery_receipt.rs` and account read documents retain separate outcomes. | Implemented: request-ID reuse checks content digest and rechecks host authorization. Acceptance is not recipient delivery or reading. Ordinary sends and integration requests have distinct entry points. |
+| Removal, recall and cleanup | `core/node/account_documents/personal.rs` represents Delete, Reopen and Applied controls; sibling history import consumes their permission cut. `node/recall.rs` owns a different operation. | Implemented: hidden state, history clearing, deletion floor and local cleanup completion are distinct. No global deletion or safe marker reclamation claim. |
+| Disclosure and local integration access | `core/node/privacy_routes.rs` provides historical route hints; authenticated transport verifies identity. `src-tauri/src/integrations.rs` adapts the integration service; MCP is a separate transport adapter. | Route hints are not proof. Grant expiry, destination rights and exact-session authority must be checked at acceptance, not inferred from a UI state or discovery result. See [integration contracts](bot-integrations.md). |
+
+### Stores and resource ownership
+
+Retain the existing [storage architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and
+[performance requirements](performance-requirements.md); this map proposes no
+migration or new cache. Storage format presence is not a performance diagnosis.
+
+| Category | Current owner and real consumer | Resource/recovery boundary and next evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Profile identity and encrypted indexed data | `core/storage/profile/`, `storage/database.rs`; event repository and transcript repository consume the profile connection. | SQLCipher owns connection/cache/WAL settings. Production and test KDF settings differ; F03 must record resolved build features before startup measurements. Per-connection cache limits are not process memory limits. |
+| Signed events and transcript projections | `core/eventlog/repository/`, `eventlog/persist.rs`, `node/transcript_repository/`; history, sync and search consume them. | Transcript headers and bodies are separate; page admission bounds rows and bytes. Legacy import code remains in `eventlog/persist/legacy.rs`; it is not evidence that every current query uses legacy storage. F03 measures metadata scans separately from decoded payloads. |
+| Durable outgoing state | `core/node/delivery_store.rs` consumes encrypted record logs for journal and outbox; delivery runtime and receipts consume transitions. | Coexists with indexed storage. F04 must qualify interrupted acceptance/reopen and sender-state recovery before any extraction or compaction. |
+| Personal controls and replay evidence | `core/node/account_documents/personal.rs`, `account_sync/`; account-history import consumes deletion floors and source cuts. | Keep replay suppression until its owning contract permits reclamation. F04 qualifies restart/restore and genuinely new content separately. |

+| UI state and transient projections | `ui/store/chat.ts`, `ownership.ts`, conversation components; host events and typed API results are inputs. | Generation checks prevent stale publication but do not establish backend cancellation. set -euo pipefail

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$repo_root"

preflight_args=()
affected_args=()
full_preflight=0
separator=0
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
        separator=1
        shift
        break
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--full-preflight" ]; then
        full_preflight=1
        shift
        continue
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--owner" ] || [ "$1" = "--reason" ]; then
        if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "$1 requires a literal value." >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        affected_args+=("$1" "$2")
        shift 2
        continue
    fi
    preflight_args+=("$1")
    shift
done
if [ "$separator" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: scripts/create-pr.sh [--full-preflight] [--owner ID --reason TEXT] [preflight selectors and UI specs] -- [gh pr create options]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ -n "${GH_REPO:-}" ]; then
    echo "Unset GH_REPO: verified PR creation uses this checkout's repository." >&2
    exit 2
fi
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --head|--head=*|-H*|--repo|--repo=*|-R*|--base|--base=*|-B*)
            echo "Head/repository overrides are forbidden. Select the shared comparison/PR base before --." >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
done

# Bash 3.2 treats an empty array as unset under nounset.
base_ref="$(node --input-type=module - ${preflight_args[@]+"${preflight_args[@]}"} <<'JS'
import { parseFlags } from './scripts/pr-platform/plan.mjs';
const flags = parseFlags(['--base', process.env.PATCH_COVERAGE_BASE ?? 'origin/main', ...process.argv.slice(2)]);
if (flags.planOnly) throw Error('Preview with scripts/pr-platform/run.mjs --plan; creation publishes a PR.');
console.log(flags.base);
JS
)"
case "$base_ref" in
    origin/*) pr_base="${base_ref#origin/}" ;;
    *)
        echo "The PR base must be an origin/<branch> tracking ref, not a local revision." >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
esac
git check-ref-format --branch "$pr_base" >/dev/null

base_sha="$(git rev-parse --verify "$base_ref")"
candidate="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
    echo "Commit or stash changes before creating a PR." >&2
    exit 1
fi
git diff --check "$base_ref"...HEAD

# Git Commit Standards for Mesh-Talk

To maintain clear and consistent commit history, we follow professional Git commit standards.

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

## Commit Types

- `feat`: New feature
- `fix`: Bug fix
- `bug`: Bug fix (synonymous with `fix`)
- `docs`: Documentation update
- `style`: Code formatting adjustment
- `refactor`: Code refactoring
- `perf`: Performance optimization
- `test`: Test-related
- `build`: Build system or external dependency changes
- `ci`: CI configuration files and script changes
- `chore`: Other changes that don't modify src or test files
- `revert`: Rollback previous commit

## Scope

Scope should identify the component or module affected by the commit:

- `network`
- `crypto`
- `ui`
- `db`
- `core`
- `cli`
- `tests`
- `config`

## Commit Message Standards

1. Write commit messages in English
2. First line is a brief description (<72 characters)
3. Second line must be a genuine blank line
4. Third line onwards is detailed description (optional)
5. Detailed description can include change reasons, impact scope, and other information
6. Make sure not to include temporary files generated during builds

## Examples

```
feat(discovery): sign UDP announce and group devices by account

- Add Ed25519 signature over the announce payload
- Carry the device certificate and verify it against the account key
- Group discovered devices by account in the roster
```

```
fix(ratchet): resolve session establishment failure

- Fix race condition in double ratchet initialization
- Add proper error handling for key exchange failures
- Update unit tests to cover edge cases
```

## Signing & Hooks

Commits **must be GPG-signed**. `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` (run by `make dev`) points
`core.hooksPath` at `hooks/` and enables `commit.gpgsign`; the `pre-push` hook rejects any
commit lacking a `gpgsig`. The `pre-commit` hook checks staged whitespace and
source formatting, ownership, hygiene and changed-script/workflow syntax; run
affected tests during development and the required gates before merge. Hook
installation does not run comprehensive health. Generate a key with `gpg --full-generate-key` and set it via
`git config --global user.signingkey <KEY_ID>` if you don't have one.

## Pull Request Merge Strategy

When the user asks to merge a pull request, use **squash merge by default**
(`gh pr merge --squash <PR>`), unless the user explicitly requests another
strategy. Use a clear Conventional Commit title and a final message describing
the completed change rather than its intermediate debugging history.

A merge request authorizes the merge only after the current PR head passes all
required checks and repository review requirements. Recheck the exact head before
merging; local checks, earlier green runs and the default strategy do not bypass
those gates. Follow the repository's worktree cleanup and branch-preservation
rules after integration.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultrathink this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

name: systematic-debugging
description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
---

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultrathink this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

# Development roadmap and requirements

## Plan ownership and execution boundary

This is the maintained global plan for the thirty user-supplied requirements,
REQ-001–REQ-030. It owns consolidation, priority, dependencies, phase exits,
readiness, task claims and future directions. The original intake is provenance,
not a competing execution backlog. The complete source mapping below preserves
all thirty requirements. The previous T-numbered execution proposal is superseded;
its numbers or historical claims are not evidence of readiness in this plan.
Existing work owned by other sessions must still be checked before claiming a task.

The delivery order is **foundations → integrated foundation acceptance → current
IM improvements → separately activated future features**. Performance, security,
verification and maintained decisions apply throughout. Forum, mobile PWA,
marketplace, external SDK and other extensions are not current assignments.

This planning change updates [agent rules](../AGENTS.md) and this roadmap together.
It must pass the existing PR/review/current-head gates and merge into `main`
before execution starts. After merge, read the accepted main revision afresh,
claim F01 and follow the dependency rules below. A planning merge does not prove
that foundations, measurements or product acceptance are complete. No public
release or product implementation belongs in the planning PR.

[Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md) owns implemented capabilities;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation responsibilities.
Existing topic guides retain authority over product/security/resource rules.
Do not invent historical rationale, measurements, deadlines or effort estimates.
Unknown implementation facts are explicit inputs to bounded investigations.

## Priority and readiness

| Priority     | Scope                                                                             | Admission rule                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0           | F01–F10: finite foundations for current IM, including performance and validation. | First F01; then independent evidence/contract lanes; construction follows accepted relevant inputs. Verified urgent security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects override normal order. |
| P1           | M01–M04: practical current-messenger improvements after foundation acceptance.    | F10 and each task's product/interface decisions accepted; independent ready tasks may run together.                                                                                   |
| Roadmap only | Future capabilities and conditional platform replacements.                        | No implementation claim until a concrete scenario, product decision, relevant contract, budget and first-slice acceptance are recorded. Their dependencies do not enlarge P0.         |

Priority is program order, not a claim that every foundation change has identical
risk/value. Within construction, rank findings by measured user impact, correctness
risk and enabling value. Choose retain/qualify, targeted fix, feature or experiment
from evidence. A no-change decision can satisfy a task when its acceptance is met;
otherwise name the unverified scenario and keep it open.

## Delivery policy

1. Define a finite foundation scope around current IM scenarios and real reuse.
   Do not implement speculative forum, browser or SDK architecture in advance.
2. Establish reproducible correctness and performance evidence before selecting
   major optimization, module extraction, database or UI changes.
3. Make boundaries useful: one policy owner, explicit inputs/results/errors,
   lifecycle and cancellation, durable commit authority and bounded resource use.
   A file split alone is not a completed module boundary.
4. Deliver and validate small changes to existing consumers. Preserve identity,
   privacy, wire/storage compatibility, delivery and recovery guarantees.
5. Accept the agreed foundation release before opening feature development.
   Severe verified security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects take precedence
   whenever discovered. Optional future ideas do not extend the foundation gate.
6. Keep performance, verification and decision records active throughout later
   work. Foundation acceptance does not mean these concerns are permanently done.

## Phases and exit criteria

| Phase                                 | Purpose and scope                                                                                                                | Exit evidence                                                                                                                                                           | Parallelism                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0. Bound the foundations              | F01: current concepts, owners, consumers, stores and critical scenarios; identify gaps without assuming defects.                 | Accepted responsibility map, existing/reusable/unknown distinctions, bounded foundation scope and authoritative guide for each work package.                            | Read-only inventories may run independently; one coordinator reconciles shared concepts.                         |
| 1. Establish evidence and contracts   | F02 verification baseline, F03 runtime baseline, F04 authority/lifecycle/interface contracts.                                    | Reproducible scenarios, representative timing/failure evidence, correctness checks and a ranked, scoped foundation change list. Unknowns have an owner and next action. | F02/F03/F04 can proceed together after relevant F01 inputs. Measurement windows stay free from build/test noise. |
| 2. Build and optimize the foundations | F05 module boundaries, F06 events/scheduling, F07 communication/sync, F08 storage/lifecycles; F09 protects each delivered slice. | Current consumers use accepted boundaries; selected costs improve or current behavior is retained with evidence; failure/recovery and compatibility remain qualified.   | Integrate F05 interfaces incrementally, then admit independent F06/F07/F08 slices. F09 accompanies every slice.  |
| 3. Accept the foundation release      | F10: qualify the agreed current-IM scenarios across the affected boundaries.                                                     | Foundation acceptance checklist met; severe risks resolved; remaining bounded gaps explicitly accepted or owned. No implied public release or publication.              | Independent acceptance scenarios may run together if their environments and data do not interfere.               |
| 4. Improve the current messenger      | Approved monitoring UI, practical anti-harassment, manual QR and package-size slices.                                            | Each feature meets its own contract, failure/recovery and resource criteria using the accepted foundations.                                                             | Separate feature lanes after F10, with one owner for any shared interface.                                       |
| Future roadmap                        | Browser review, meetings, PWA, forum/feed, alternative clients/market, external SDK and incentives.                              | Separate product decision, relevant foundation evidence and an independently testable first slice before activation.                                                    | No current assignments. Future independent features may run together after their own gates.                      |

Phase progression is evidence-based, not calendar-based. Existing working
capabilities can satisfy a package through inspection and qualification; every
package is not a mandate to replace its implementation.

## Foundation work packages and dependencies

F identifiers name the foundation program. They do not convert previous task
states. All tasks begin **unclaimed and unstarted** until the execution cycle
begins from the merged planning baseline. A dependency requires an accepted
relevant output, not the completion of an unrelated whole document or subsystem.
For construction packages, select one bounded real-consumer slice per delivery
branch; a broad package is not permission for an all-app rewrite.

| Package                                             | Outcome / scope                                                                                                                                                                          | Required inputs                                                                                               | Acceptance / boundary                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F01 — Concepts and responsibility map               | Explain current business concepts, module responsibilities, real callers, stores and extension points. Identify authoritative rules and existing evidence.                               | The thirty source requirements and later authorized implementation inspection.                                | Each foundation package has an owner, real consumers, invariant and inspection gap; no blanket refactor or duplicated inventory.                                                                          |
| F02 — Effective and timely verification             | Map local/CI/native/release checks; measure waiting, setup, compilation, execution, failures and retries; assess actual assertion gaps.                                                  | Relevant F01 ownership and scenarios.                                                                         | A reproducible baseline and check-allocation proposal preserving meaningful failure detection. Evaluate supplied methods explicitly; not every tool becomes a mandatory gate.                             |
| F03 — Runtime baseline and attribution              | Measure startup, idle, active IM and return to idle, including app-related processes, CPU/memory/disk/network and available energy/wakeup evidence. Inventory reusable observations.     | Relevant F01 workload/store/process owners.                                                                   | Comparable build/platform/data/window provenance, resource attribution, ranked findings and measurement limits. No assumption that timers, SQLite or UI technology are the root cause.                    |
| F04 — Authority, lifecycle and interface contracts  | Specify identity/privacy/permissions, personal and group sync, announcement/member distinctions, pending/effective state, retention/deletion/recovery and operation lifetime.            | Relevant F01 ownership and current behavior inspection.                                                       | Resolve rules needed by the selected foundation slices; name remaining decisions. Business-specific authority stays explicit. No preselected Raft, global deletion, anonymity or external SDK.            |
| F05 — Useful module boundaries                      | Clarify/extract the necessary interfaces and migrate actual existing consumers. Separate core policy, host adaptation and presentation; define transport/sync/business responsibilities. | Relevant F01/F04 outputs, an adequate F02 safety check and F03 baseline for affected performance paths.       | One authoritative policy owner, explicit errors/cancellation/commit boundary and tested real consumers. Retain good existing seams. No SDK packaging or cosmetic file-count target.                       |
| F06 — Event and scheduling governance               | Reuse meaningful events and shared scheduling admission; remove evidenced duplicate polling/work; preserve required timeout, retry and recovery.                                         | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces used by the slice.                                            | Trigger, coalescing, bounded work, progress, cancellation and return-to-idle evidence; no duplicate legacy worker left active. A single universal scheduler is not presumed necessary.                    |
| F07 — Communication and synchronization foundations | Qualify and improve needed connection/transport/sync/delivery boundaries; personal replay, group propagation/recovery, announcements and member authority remain distinct.               | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces used by the slice.                                            | Agreed duplicate/reorder/partition/restart/revoke/compatibility scenarios with bounded resource behavior. Share transfer mechanisms without erasing business-specific permissions or merge rules.         |
| F08 — Storage and resource lifecycles               | Improve selected incremental I/O, startup/history/search, cache/memory reclamation, retention/capacity and deletion behavior.                                                            | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces; accepted F07 rules for sync-range/deletion-dependent slices. | Measured targeted costs and repeated recovery/return-to-idle checks. Separate local visibility, durable deletion, account decisions and recall. Marker reclamation requires safe replay/restore evidence. |
| F09 — Regression protection and maintained rules    | Bind each foundation change to reusable correctness/performance scenarios, efficient validation selection, AI reuse guidance and supported decision rationale.                           | F02/F03/F04 plus each selected F05–F08 delivery.                                                              | Tests detect relevant failures, resource observations are attributable, selectors/docs match behavior and recurring verification cost is recorded. Deliver continuously, not as a final testing backlog.  |
| F10 — Foundation acceptance                         | Integrate accepted packages and verify current IM behavior, performance, authority, lifecycle and reuse on the agreed source/platform scope.                                             | Accepted F01–F09 outputs for the agreed scope.                                                                | The checklist below is satisfied. This gate opens feature planning/development; it does not publish a build or complete future features.                                                                  |

### Sequencing within foundation construction

- Start with F01, then prepare F02/F03/F04 in parallel. Do not wait for an
  elaborate monitoring UI to collect performance evidence.
- Select the smallest useful F05 boundary changes. Publish their contract and
  migration order before other packages change the same callers or state owners.
- F06/F07/F08 can overlap once their required interface slices are accepted.
  Communication correctness improvements may proceed independently from history
  pagination; deletion semantics cannot proceed independently from replay rules.
- Pair each module/interface change with qualification of its existing consumer;
  optimize measured costs in the same or a following bounded slice. Do not defer
  every performance improvement until after an app-wide refactor.
- Deliver F09 with each slice. Assess F10 only after all mandatory scoped
  foundation outputs are accepted. Reopen an upstream contract deliberately when
  evidence invalidates it; do not silently patch incompatible rules downstream.

## Execution waves and concrete handoffs

After the planning PR merges, use these waves for dispatch. Each accepted output
is reusable; no lane must finish an exhaustive survey before another lane can
make a bounded change. Current claims remain separate from this readiness map.

| Wave                                  | Work admitted                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Required handoff before the next wave                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A. Bound the current-IM program       | F01: identify account/device/session meanings, current messaging/sync/file/history flows, storage categories and real owners.
