# Makefile for Mesh-Talk

# Development commands
.PHONY: dev build pr-check test test-focused test-plan test-changed verify-plan verify-changed version-check version-sync version-prepare standards-check validation-report validation-audit test-timing e2e eval-smoke ai-eval smoke-full clean clean-builds clean-builds-dry-run check

# Managed commands coordinate with cache eviction across all local worktrees.
MANAGED_BUILD = python3 scripts/build-retention.py run --

dev: install-deps frontend-install
	@echo "Development environment configured!"
	./scripts/setup-hooks.sh
	./scripts/install-auto-clean-macos.sh

build:
	python3 scripts/build-retention.py run --archive binary -- cargo build --release

test:
	$(MANAGED_BUILD) node scripts/validation/stage.mjs workspace-tests --profile shared --resource heavy -- cargo test --workspace

# Normal development: select the affected crate and test filter, or one integration
# target. Keep `make test` as the explicit comprehensive pre-PR/CI command.
test-focused:
	@test -n "$(TEST_PACKAGE)" && { test -n "$(TEST_FILTER)" || test -n "$(TEST_TARGET)"; } || { echo "Usage: make test-focused TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync [TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan]" >&2; exit 2; }
	@if [ -n "$(TEST_TARGET)" ]; then \
		$(MANAGED_BUILD) node scripts/validation/stage.mjs rust-focused --profile shared --resource heavy -- cargo test -p "$(TEST_PACKAGE)" --test "$(TEST_TARGET)" "$(TEST_FILTER)"; \
	else \
		$(MANAGED_BUILD) node scripts/validation/stage.mjs rust-focused --profile shared --resource heavy -- cargo test -p "$(TEST_PACKAGE)" --lib "$(TEST_FILTER)"; \
	fi

# Development-only affected tests. Preview first; pass literal planner options with
# VALIDATION_ARGS (for example --base origin/main). Required PR gates are unchanged.
test-plan:
	node scripts/validation/changed.mjs $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

test-changed:
	$(MANAGED_BUILD) node scripts/validation/changed.mjs --run $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

# Cheap PR preparation: static/policy checks, no application suites or builds.
pr-check:
	node scripts/validation/changed.mjs --cheap --base origin/main $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

verify-plan:
	node scripts/validation/changed.mjs --checks $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

verify-changed:
	node scripts/validation/changed.mjs --checks --run --managed $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

version-check:
	node scripts/release/version.mjs check

version-sync:
	node scripts/release/version.mjs sync

version-prepare:
	@test -n "$(VERSION)" || { echo "Usage: make version-prepare VERSION=0.x.y" >&2; exit 2; }
	node scripts/release/version.mjs prepare "$(VERSION)"

standards-check:
	node scripts/validation/standards.mjs

validation-report:
	@node scripts/validation/latency.mjs $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

validation-audit:
	@node scripts/validation/selection-audit.mjs $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

test-timing:
	@node scripts/validation/libtest-timing.mjs $(VALIDATION_ARGS)

# End-to-end integration tests: real `mesh-talk-node` processes over UDP discovery +
# TCP (two-node DM, history-across-restart, post-office offline delivery,
# and opt-in cross-LAN bridge discovery). `#[ignore]`d
# by default (real UDP-multicast discovery + node cold starts), so run them explicitly here. Serial
# (--test-threads=1) to avoid discovery-port / CPU contention between the heavy processes.

# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.
For producer/consumer artifact handoffs, pass the successful upload's immutable
artifact ID instead of rediscovering it by name. Keep source, run, attempt and
content-digest validation at the consumer; an artifact ID alone is not acceptance.
Release evidence recording and upload retain their verified-draft prerequisite but run
after final publication failure or cancellation. Keep failure summaries actionable and
source-bound. Nonpublishing branch runs retain workflow-artifact evidence without requiring
a draft. Retained evidence from a failed run is diagnostic; the verified-build owner
still requires successful exact-source jobs/run before authorizing reuse. The existing
release-gates and release-reuse regressions own these producer/consumer boundaries.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).

Budget hosted job envelopes for cold source builds, scenario execution, evidence
publication and cache cleanup together. Keep build-command and business-scenario
watchdogs independent; successful assertions can still leave an unsuccessful job
when post-actions exceed its envelope. Inspect the timed-out phase and its
measurements before changing a deadline.

Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Keep workflow policy thin and reject cheap failures locally

Workflows own triggers, permissions, runners, matrices, dependencies and artifact
transport. Scripts own inventory validation, artifact roles, packaging, report
collection and execution policy. Reuse the same CLI locally and in Actions;
extract substantial conditionals and loops into the existing feature owner rather
than copying YAML fragments or introducing another generic orchestration layer.
When moving execution into a script, update every caller and smoke check. Keep
launcher behavior in its owning regression instead of requiring obsolete command
text in YAML. Cross-platform filesystem paths use `fileURLToPath` rather than
`.pathname`; ESM module arguments retain a file URL or relative module specifier
instead of a native Windows absolute path. Exercise each boundary on its platform.
Keep live source/release checks immediately before each publication boundary;
those protect against changed state and are not redundant setup checks.

Consolidate pure checks only when their immutable candidate, scope and inputs are
identical. Health's full-scope Linux portable job owns source standards and Git
index hygiene after frontend dependency setup; documentation scope retains its
independent source gate. Real checker portability fixtures still run on every
Health platform. Native CI alone supplies partial acceptance: the protected
current-source Health check in the UI workflow and the complete release source
check closure remain necessary. Keep checks at distinct candidate, artifact,
trust or runtime boundaries, including archive producer and consumer identity and
cleanliness checks. Removing repeated source invocations does not establish a
hosted speedup; measure runner cost and latency separately.

The [syntax owner](../scripts/validation/syntax.mjs) parses changed Node, Bash and
Python sources without executing them or writing Python caches, and invokes
`actionlint` for changed workflows. Pre-commit selects staged paths but checks
worktree bytes, matching the existing structural checks. Affected validation also
checks new nonignored sources; PR creation checks the clean committed comparison.
Use Node 22, Bash and Python; install actionlint before changing workflows. No
checker installs tools or contacts the network. Hook installation configures hooks
without launching comprehensive health; request that gate explicitly.
Run the configured spelling check on changed files before publication, and scan
the repository when its configuration changes. Scope unavoidable external API
spellings to their language and identifier; do not exclude a source tree or
replace the API name to satisfy a prose checker.

PR creation runs `make pr-check`'s cheap-check owner against its actual comparison
base, rejects ownership blockers and checks applicable frontend patch coverage
before publication. The creation wrapper accepts repeated `--owner ID` and
`--reason TEXT` before `--` and forwards them only to that existing affected-plan
owner. Review every otherwise unmapped path before making this explicit selection;
it records responsibility, not test acceptance. Platform selectors remain separate,
and missing/invalid owners, absent reasons and checker failures still block creation.
Version projections, contract references and hygiene already
belong to structural standards; reuse that owner rather than adding duplicate
gates. Do not install dependencies, compile Rust, launch browsers or run application suites
implicitly in the cheap mode. Source changes during checking invalidate it.
Workflow edits also run the existing fast CI policy owner locally. Configuration
assertions and runner inventory discovery belong here; application execution and
native compiler fixtures do not. Keep static policy assertions independently runnable
without native tool setup. Scope fixture configuration changes to their owning
table or profile; repeated valid values elsewhere must remain unchanged. Update the existing policy assertion when its
requirement changes instead of adding a second overlapping test in another file.
Write generated reports into the task-owned evidence directory, not the source
checkout. Fixtures for source-integrity checks must preserve production ignore
rules; adding a fixture-only ignore can hide a real dirty-worktree failure.
For entry-point changes, also run the affected contract tests selected by the
existing validation plan before publication. A syntax pass or a hand-picked
filename sample cannot detect stale semantic routing expectations; cheap PR
checks do not certify those tests passed.

The frontend precheck reads the target from `codecov.yml`, includes partially
covered branches in the uncovered denominator and rejects omitted changed files.
Exercise report readers against actual producer output as well as small fixtures;
negative V8 branch counts remain uncovered rather than invalidating the report.
It verifies an existing clean-candidate `frontend-coverage` receipt through the
canonical stage owner and rechecks LCOV bytes, rather than trusting a timestamp or
raw report. Generate missing evidence explicitly with the reported command. A
verification-only miss never starts coverage, waits for a heavy lock or claims a
pass; a no-work verification lease must not imply admitted child work. Keep
verified scope termination diagnostics separate from the actual test result.
This frontend unit precheck is conservative; Rust and browser-union coverage
still need their owning evidence. Native execution, dependency resolution and
published-asset verification cannot be replaced by parsing or stale build output.

Use the existing package inventory's `frontendBuild` ownership when preparing
Rust selectors. Core, integrations and MCP selections still require real target
validation, but do not build frontend assets merely because Rust changed. Host
selections must still prepare Tauri's `frontendDist` before selector discovery.

Composed local gates must invoke shared stages through the same canonical command
and full-mode environment. Normalize `FAST=0` in both full-preflight children so
equivalent successful stages can reuse their verified receipts; do not weaken
identity checks or mutate the caller's environment to manufacture a cache hit.

[workspace]
members = ["crates/mesh-talk-core", "crates/mesh-talk-integrations", "crates/mesh-talk-mcp", "src-tauri"]
resolver = "3"

# Layered workspace:
#   crates/mesh-talk-core — the UI-free protocol core (the SDK foundation)
#   crates/mesh-talk-integrations — scoped local service and dedicated bot host
#   crates/mesh-talk-mcp   — MCP adapter over the local service
#   src-tauri             — the Tauri desktop app, a thin shell over the core
# Shared package metadata + dependency versions live here so the crates never
# drift apart. Each crate opts in with `<dep>.workspace = true`.

[workspace.package]
version = "0.4.6"
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk"

# Lint guardrails shared by all crates (each opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`).
# These are enforced by `cargo clippy` locally (make lint / pre-commit) and in CI.
[workspace.lints.clippy]
# Lock-correctness: holding a std Mutex/RwLock guard across an `.await` can deadlock
# the async runtime (the guard isn't released while the task is parked). The audit's
# P5 fixed the existing cases; `deny` keeps any new one out.
await_holding_lock = "deny"
# Performance: flag accidentally-huge async state machines (a large future moved
# around / boxed on every poll). `warn` — informational, not gating.
large_futures = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Async + serialization
tokio = { version = "1.28", features = ["full"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
bincode = "1.3"
# Logging
log = "0.4.28"
tracing = "0.1.41"
# Encoding
base64 = "0.23"
hex = "0.4"
uuid = { version = "1.0", features = ["v4", "serde"] }
# Cryptography
aes-gcm = "0.11"
pbkdf2 = "0.12"
sha2 = "0.10"
hkdf = "0.12"
ed25519-dalek = "3.0"
x25519-dalek = { version = "3", features = ["static_secrets", "getrandom"] }
snow = "0.9"
zeroize = "1"
argon2 = { version = "0.5", features = ["std"] }
# Keep the existing rand_core 0.6 entropy API; key constructors consume raw bytes.
# Desktop token generation and deterministic property tests use their own RNG versions.
rand_core = { version = "0.6", features = ["getrandom"] }
# Networking
socket2 = { version = "0.6", features = ["all"] }
if-addrs = "0.15"
# CLI
clap = { version = "4.4", features = ["derive"] }
# Misc
lazy_static = "1.4"
# Dev
tempfile = "3.8"

# Mutation testing rebuilds once per injected bug; symbols add cost without useful
# diagnostics for these expected failures. Normal dev/test profiles stay unchanged.
[profile.mutants]
inherits = "test"
debug = "none"
incremental = true

# Keep the default speed-oriented opt-level while reducing duplicate native code and
# shipping symbols. Thin LTO limits release build time compared with fat LTO.
[profile.release]
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"

# The Tauri shell dominates local release rebuilds. Split only this crate's
# code generation across cores; keep dependencies and the protocol core at one
# unit for their existing release-size/runtime trade-off. Thin LTO and symbol
# stripping still apply to the final app.
[profile.release.package.mesh-talk]
codegen-units = 4

# Dev-build ergonomics: full-strength Argon2/PBKDF2 are unbearably slow in an unoptimized
# debug build — `tauri dev` keystore unlock ("unlocking your encrypted stores") can take
# minutes and looks like a hang. Optimize crypto dependencies so unlock is fast;
# most application crates keep default debug optimization for incremental builds.
# KDF parameters stay unchanged, so existing keystores decrypt. Release builds are unaffected.
[profile.dev.package.argon2]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.blake2]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.pbkdf2]

# Quality gates and release evidence

The gate verifies outcomes, not just process exit codes. A successful compiler,
high line coverage, or a browser mock is not proof of a correct native release.
Keep implementation plans and transient verification logs outside the repository.

## Change review

Prefer independently reviewable PRs with one feature or mechanism. Record the exact
tested commit, executed commands, failing-baseline evidence, native runner links,
and limitations in the PR. Follow the [validation stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
for affected feedback and boundary evidence; comprehensive local preparation is
optional, and current-candidate protected CI remains required before merge.
Use the existing [PR preparation entry point](testing-feedback-loop.md#fast-pr-creation-and-optional-full-local-preparation)
when comprehensive local evidence is needed. The full health gate builds frontend
assets before Tauri compilation, including on a fresh checkout.

[CI maintenance](ci-maintenance.md) owns efficiency and reliability decisions.
Gate scope, evidence requirements and release acceptance remain owned here;
an optimization proposal does not itself authorize reducing them.

For each applicable scenario, assert externally observable outcomes. A test should
fail with the old implementation or a deliberate incorrect mutation. Do not weaken
assertions to accommodate unexplained failures.

| Change                 | Required scenarios in addition to the happy path                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Persistent state       | Reopen/restart, append after torn record, read/write failure, owner isolation, no memory-only success after failed persistence |
| Permissions/privacy    | Allow and deny, revocation after existing session, restart recovery, unknown peer/device, group vs direct-message boundaries   |
| Async UI/media         | Account switch/logout while request is pending, late response rejection, failed save and retry, media cleanup                  |
| Multiple devices/files | Every destination, one logical history record, sender restart before recipient download, revoked access                        |
| Platform/native UI     | Real Tauri IPC and window/process state on the affected OS, negative control, runner/desktop/GPU limitations                   |
| CI/release scripts     | Real fixture files, missing/partial evidence, tool failures, changed source and stale artifacts                                |

Rust unit/integration, real multi-process backend E2E, browser UI tests, and native
desktop tests answer different questions. A VM/Xvfb/software-renderer pass does not
establish that a reported physical GPU or VMware compositor fault is fixed.

A clean exact-current-main promotion into dev may use the
[trusted main synchronization proof](ci-maintenance.md#synchronizing-an-accepted-main-source-into-dev)
for PR preparation. Its source must already satisfy the existing complete trusted
main-push acceptance owner, and dev still requires its own integration checks.
Ordinary source changes retain the configured local patch coverage target.

## Test quality and evidence

`node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs` runs in three-platform CI and the health
gate. Python 3.11+ is required for archive regressions; CI pins Python 3.12. The
diagnostic suite includes actual release-script execution with deliberate verifier
failures, real ZIP corruption fixtures, and release-state changes after verification.
Full health requires cargo-deny, cargo-machete, typos, Gitleaks, ShellCheck and
actionlint; missing tools fail rather than being silently skipped. CI installs them
explicitly. `--fast` remains a clearly labeled partial local check.

For full-scope candidates, Health runs inside the UI orchestrator for every PR and
merge candidate, and independently on its weekly/manual triggers. All three
platform diagnostic suites remain mandatory. The complete frontend unit suite
runs once with coverage on Linux; its platform branches use explicit mocks,
while real browser/native behavior retains the platform matrices. Source-only
formatting, type/lint and dependency policy run once. The Linux coverage producer seals
its line map for same-run UI consumers; source, workflow, run, attempt and digest
must all match. Superseded PR and merge candidates are cancelled automatically. Every main push
has its own verification group, preserving pending commits for release evidence.
Health uses a distinct caller-workflow/event namespace, so independent manual or
scheduled runs cannot cancel the UI caller or its same-run evidence producer.

Inert documentation PRs may omit unrelated product execution only after the
[documentation scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
proves eligibility against the exact tested merge. Required check identities
remain present and validate that decision; their success means the product work
is not applicable, not that its tests ran. Applicable documentation and security
checks still run. Failed selection, mixed changes and authority inputs cannot
qualify. Main pushes, merge groups, schedules and manual runs retain complete
execution. Release consumers require checks from the owning successful trusted
main-push workflow suite, never PR-only scope decisions.

Main branch protection requires direct execution checks instead of runner-backed
copies of their aggregate result. `scripts/ci/required-checks.mjs` owns the direct
release policy and replacement mapping. Development-only dependency profiles use the
[exact-merge CI scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#dependabot-development-acceptance)
and retain the existing `dev` required `verify` compatibility context, whose Linux
producer requires actual selected npm acceptance. That exception cannot authorize
main or release acceptance. Source and all platform checks are
individually required for main; Windows requires its build producer and all archive
consumers. Release acceptance uses the same direct names plus its main-only
checks, including ASan and mutation-runner acceptance. A newer failed, pending or
missing check still rejects the exact source. Stable repeats this strict check
immediately before public container upload and final release publication, after
lengthy preparation; Nightly retains its final strict recheck. To inspect a migration, run
`node scripts/ci/migrate-required-checks.mjs OWNER/REPO main PR_NUMBER --plan`.
Use `--apply` only after the replacement checks pass on the current PR head. The
command validates each bound GitHub App, rejects a changed candidate/policy,
preserves strictness and unrelated checks, and verifies the readback. A missing
old context before migration is pending, never permission to bypass a gate.
Diagnostics run on the actual native test machine; a probe on another VM cannot
certify that machine's network capability. Windows gates explicitly use Bash;
opening a script through a file association does not establish execution.

Mutation testing uses pinned cargo-mutants 27.1.0 and examines all Rust workspace
members on daily and manual runs. PR, push and merge-queue runs validate the pinned
runner with real fixture crates; they do not sample product mutations. See the
[mutation execution policy](testing-feedback-loop.md) for ownership and budgets.
Each broad run rotates through one of 256 round-robin samples. The existing
[mutation evidence owner](../scripts/release/mutation-evidence.mjs) partitions
that exact selected set into bounded chunks; worker count may grow without
changing the sample. Each worker retains one in-place mutation process,
incremental compilation, the symbol-free `mutants` Cargo profile and the existing
workspace-root cache. Every mutant still tests the complete workspace through the
pinned cargo-nextest runner. Scheduling and deadlines belong to that owner, the
[Nextest profile](../.config/nextest.toml) and the workflow rather than duplicated
numeric assumptions in documentation.

Deep runs execute one complete unmutated workspace baseline before admitting
workers. Its receipt must attest actual successful execution, complete inventory,
source, configuration and tool identities. Workers verify the immutable artifact
against trusted current-run producer outputs before skipping their own inline
baseline. A successful producer from an earlier attempt of the same run may be
reused by a failed-only rerun; another source or run cannot qualify it. Raw
cargo-mutants reports in this mode must contain no inline `Baseline` outcome;
never fabricate one. Shared execution uses the Linux kernel owner for separately grouped tool work;
normal exit, cancellation and build cleanup must verify complete retirement before
any baseline or worker result is sealed. Missing acknowledgment is incomplete
evidence. Ordinary portable inline baseline execution remains supported.
Empty selections validate selection/tooling only and do not constitute baseline
evidence. Assess the baseline receipt and every planned worker report together.

Selected counts, completed outcomes, baseline evidence, tool exits and summary
counts must agree. A zero selection is recorded explicitly and may have no report;
a stale report is rejected. Real dependency-free fixtures exercise the pinned CLI,
caught/advisory outcomes, baseline failure, empty selection, hanging mutations
and shared-baseline rejection through
`node --test scripts/release/run-mutants.test.mjs`. Individual process watchdogs
remain distinct from the complete-suite deadline: intentional hanging-mutant
controls retain the pinned tool's caught classification, while a failed baseline
or inconclusive tool-level timeout never qualifies acceptance.

Survivors remain advisory and must be triaged in review. Unviable mutants are not
caught mutants. Timeouts, usage/diff/internal errors, absent reports and incomplete
sweeps fail the job: they are inconclusive, not successful validation. The full sweep
still has a runtime budget; a timed-out sweep is not represented as complete.
Report formats and exit codes follow [cargo-mutants documentation](https://mutants.rs/mutants-out.html)
and [the pinned exit-code definitions](https://github.com/sourcefrog/cargo-mutants/blob/v27.1.0/src/exit_code.rs).

Coverage remains a signal, not a substitute for assertions or mutation review. Do
not count test-module lines as production-only coverage, unviable mutants as killed,
or skipped/inconclusive native scenarios as passed.

## Release workflow
# Core workflow and platform evaluations

Product evaluations are separate from prompt/agent/model evaluations. A successful
build, coverage percentage, PNG file signature or mocked browser session alone is
not evidence that the shipped desktop workflow works.

## Layers and honest boundaries

The protected CI matrix runs Rust workspace unit/integration tests and frontend
Vitest unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows. Linux records Rust `llvm-cov` and
frontend V8 coverage; the frontend report includes every production `.ts` and
`.tsx` file, including files with zero unit coverage. The `src/store` line gate
is 70%. Run `cd frontend && npm run test:coverage` locally to inspect the
frontend report in `frontend/coverage/`. Browser and native E2E assertions do
not contribute to this unit coverage percentage, so low component percentages
must be read alongside the scenario matrix below.

| Layer            | Systems exercised                                                                                                                    | Platforms                                                  | Boundary                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Backend core     | Real CLI processes, signed discovery, encrypted TCP, DM/channel delivery, process restart, relay delivery, received file bytes       | Linux, Windows, macOS                                      | No renderer; discovery can use its signed unicast fallback, so a passed scenario does not prove multicast-only discovery             |
| Native core      | Actual Tauri builder/webview, embedded dev-only W3C driver, real CLI peer, persisted production stores, native keyboard/dialog input | Linux GTK/WebKit, Windows WebView2, macOS WKWebView/AppKit | No IPC replacement; test example uses existing cheap test KDF, separately built CLI and production application retain production KDF |
| Portable browser | Real React UI and visible interactions with a deterministic mocked IPC/event boundary                                                | Chromium on Linux/Windows/macOS; WebKit on macOS           | Guards UI wiring/layout, not native transport, OS chrome or Rust authentication                                                      |
| Model-backed AI  | External model responses scored against prompt/agent cases                                                                           | Configured provider                                        | Not a product E2E; an unavailable provider means **not run**, never a real-model pass                                                |

Hosted runners cannot establish behavior for every physical camera, microphone,
GPU, monitor scale, compositor or LAN firewall. Those remain explicit manual
acceptance checks; do not convert unavailable devices to passing observations.

## Backend execution and evidence

Run from the repository root:

```sh
EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/mesh-talk-backend-eval node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs
```

The runner selects the four integration test targets explicitly and runs ignored
tests serially, continuing through independent suites after a failure while
retaining the overall failing verdict. It requires all five named scenarios exactly once, a matching
Cargo test count and zero failures/ignored/filtered tests. An exit-zero invocation
which selects no tests is a failure. The JSON report binds source revision,
platform, timings and SHA256 log digests. Artifacts contain test observations and
redacted logs, never fixture keystores or account directories.

Normal CLI shutdown sends `/quit` and waits for the owned child to exit before
reusing its store. The test helper never removes a child's lock to manufacture a
successful restart. Forced termination remains a separate recovery boundary,
particularly on Windows where conservative stale-lock handling needs care.

The offline relay test must stop the sender before the receiver returns. A test
with the sender still online cannot independently establish post-office delivery;
ordinary direct synchronization could satisfy the same message assertion. Failure
of this stricter route-isolated scenario must be investigated, not hidden by
relaxing it or removing it from the required matrix.

## Native scenarios and evidence

The native runner retains the 13 contact-hiding/invisible-mode scenarios and adds
registration/sign-in, logout/invalid-password recovery, signed discovery,
bidirectional DM, Unicode/multiline/long content, channel delivery, attachment
rendering, history after real process restart, theme persistence, profile/avatar
geometry and settings geometry at default and minimum window sizes.

At native app readiness, the dev-only driver also requires the handled Mesh-Talk
tray icon to exist and Tauri's unhandled default `main` tray icon to be absent.
This checks actual Tauri registration on each runner; it does not simulate an OS
tray click or inspect stale icons retained by a Windows shell after a crash.

The native menu's lifetime follows the registered tray resource. In the locked
Tauri 2.12.4 implementation, `TrayIconBuilder::menu` obtains an owned clone through
`Menu::inner_context_owned`; building the tray registers a clone in the app's
resource table and tray registry. The locked tray-icon 0.25.1 platform
implementations retain that owned menu, and muda 0.20.0 menu clones share their
native menu and child items. Dropping the local `tray_menu` variable therefore
does not release the registered menu. `TrayMenuState` retains the shared unread
item for updates; explicit tray removal or application exit ends registration.
These are dependency ownership guarantees, rather than native click evidence.
Recheck them when changing the locked versions: the owning sources are
[Tauri's tray builder and registration](https://docs.rs/tauri/2.12.4/src/tauri/tray/mod.rs.html),
[Tauri's owned menu clone](https://docs.rs/tauri/2.12.4/src/tauri/menu/menu.rs.html),
and the platform implementations in `tray-icon`'s `src/platform_impl`.

Each passing scenario supplies JSON observations, a screenshot and a redacted
process log. Schema 2 requires the tested source revision and SHA256 digests for
all three files. Validation requires typed scenario observations and fully decodes
bounded RGB/RGBA PNG pixels, rejecting corrupt, truncated, blank or transparent
screenshots. These checks prevent incomplete/stale evidence from passing; they
do not replace the scenario's interaction and layout assertions.

# Quality gates and release evidence

The gate verifies outcomes, not just process exit codes. A successful compiler,
high line coverage, or a browser mock is not proof of a correct native release.
Keep implementation plans and transient verification logs outside the repository.

## Change review

Prefer independently reviewable PRs with one feature or mechanism. Record the exact
tested commit, executed commands, failing-baseline evidence, native runner links,
and limitations in the PR. Follow the [validation stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
for affected feedback and boundary evidence; comprehensive local preparation is
optional, and current-candidate protected CI remains required before merge.
Use the existing [PR preparation entry point](testing-feedback-loop.md#fast-pr-creation-and-optional-full-local-preparation)
when comprehensive local evidence is needed. The full health gate builds frontend
assets before Tauri compilation, including on a fresh checkout.

[CI maintenance](ci-maintenance.md) owns efficiency and reliability decisions.
Gate scope, evidence requirements and release acceptance remain owned here;
an optimization proposal does not itself authorize reducing them.

For each applicable scenario, assert externally observable outcomes. A test should
fail with the old implementation or a deliberate incorrect mutation. Do not weaken
assertions to accommodate unexplained failures.

| Change                 | Required scenarios in addition to the happy path                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Persistent state       | Reopen/restart, append after torn record, read/write failure, owner isolation, no memory-only success after failed persistence |
| Permissions/privacy    | Allow and deny, revocation after existing session, restart recovery, unknown peer/device, group vs direct-message boundaries   |
| Async UI/media         | Account switch/logout while request is pending, late response rejection, failed save and retry, media cleanup                  |
| Multiple devices/files | Every destination, one logical history record, sender restart before recipient download, revoked access                        |
| Platform/native UI     | Real Tauri IPC and window/process state on the affected OS, negative control, runner/desktop/GPU limitations                   |
| CI/release scripts     | Real fixture files, missing/partial evidence, tool failures, changed source and stale artifacts                                |

Rust unit/integration, real multi-process backend E2E, browser UI tests, and native
desktop tests answer different questions. A VM/Xvfb/software-renderer pass does not
establish that a reported physical GPU or VMware compositor fault is fixed.

A clean exact-current-main promotion into dev may use the
[trusted main synchronization proof](ci-maintenance.md#synchronizing-an-accepted-main-source-into-dev)
for PR preparation. Its source must already satisfy the existing complete trusted
main-push acceptance owner, and dev still requires its own integration checks.
Ordinary source changes retain the configured local patch coverage target.

## Test quality and evidence

`node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs` runs in three-platform CI and the health
gate. Python 3.11+ is required for archive regressions; CI pins Python 3.12. The
diagnostic suite includes actual release-script execution with deliberate verifier
failures, real ZIP corruption fixtures, and release-state changes after verification.
Full health requires cargo-deny, cargo-machete, typos, Gitleaks, ShellCheck and
actionlint; missing tools fail rather than being silently skipped. CI installs them
explicitly. `--fast` remains a clearly labeled partial local check.

For full-scope candidates, Health runs inside the UI orchestrator for every PR and
merge candidate, and independently on its weekly/manual triggers. All three
platform diagnostic suites remain mandatory. The complete frontend unit suite
runs once with coverage on Linux; its platform branches use explicit mocks,
while real browser/native behavior retains the platform matrices. Source-only
formatting, type/lint and dependency policy run once. The Linux coverage producer seals
its line map for same-run UI consumers; source, workflow, run, attempt and digest
must all match. Superseded PR and merge candidates are cancelled automatically. Every main push
has its own verification group, preserving pending commits for release evidence.
Health uses a distinct caller-workflow/event namespace, so independent manual or
scheduled runs cannot cancel the UI caller or its same-run evidence producer.

Inert documentation PRs may omit unrelated product execution only after the
[documentation scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
proves eligibility against the exact tested merge. Required check identities
remain present and validate that decision; their success means the product work
is not applicable, not that its tests ran. Applicable documentation and security
checks still run. Failed selection, mixed changes and authority inputs cannot
qualify. Main pushes, merge groups, schedules and manual runs retain complete
execution. Release consumers require checks from the owning successful trusted
main-push workflow suite, never PR-only scope decisions.

Main branch protection requires direct execution checks instead of runner-backed
copies of their aggregate result. `scripts/ci/required-checks.mjs` owns the direct
release policy and replacement mapping. Development-only dependency profiles use the
[exact-merge CI scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#dependabot-development-acceptance)
and retain the existing `dev` required `verify` compatibility context, whose Linux
producer requires actual selected npm acceptance. That exception cannot authorize
main or release acceptance. Source and all platform checks are
individually required for main; Windows requires its build producer and all archive
consumers. Release acceptance uses the same direct names plus its main-only
checks, including ASan and mutation-runner acceptance. A newer failed, pending or
missing check still rejects the exact source. Stable repeats this strict check
immediately before public container upload and final release publication, after
lengthy preparation; Nightly retains its final strict recheck. To inspect a migration, run
`node scripts/ci/migrate-required-checks.mjs OWNER/REPO main PR_NUMBER --plan`.
Use `--apply` only after the replacement checks pass on the current PR head. The
command validates each bound GitHub App, rejects a changed candidate/policy,
preserves strictness and unrelated checks, and verifies the readback. A missing
old context before migration is pending, never permission to bypass a gate.
Diagnostics run on the actual native test machine; a probe on another VM cannot
certify that machine's network capability. Windows gates explicitly use Bash;
opening a script through a file association does not establish execution.

Mutation testing uses pinned cargo-mutants 27.1.0 and examines all Rust workspace
members on daily and manual runs. PR, push and merge-queue runs validate the pinned
runner with real fixture crates; they do not sample product mutations. See the
[mutation execution policy](testing-feedback-loop.md) for ownership and budgets.
Each broad run rotates through one of 256 round-robin samples. The existing
[mutation evidence owner](../scripts/release/mutation-evidence.mjs) partitions
that exact selected set into bounded chunks; worker count may grow without
changing the sample. Each worker retains one in-place mutation process,
incremental compilation, the symbol-free `mutants` Cargo profile and the existing
workspace-root cache. Every mutant still tests the complete workspace through the
pinned cargo-nextest runner. Scheduling and deadlines belong to that owner, the
[Nextest profile](../.config/nextest.toml) and the workflow rather than duplicated
numeric assumptions in documentation.

Deep runs execute one complete unmutated workspace baseline before admitting
workers. Its receipt must attest actual successful execution, complete inventory,
source, configuration and tool identities. Workers verify the immutable artifact
against trusted current-run producer outputs before skipping their own inline
baseline. A successful producer from an earlier attempt of the same run may be
reused by a failed-only rerun; another source or run cannot qualify it. Raw
cargo-mutants reports in this mode must contain no inline `Baseline` outcome;
never fabricate one. Shared execution uses the Linux kernel owner for separately grouped tool work;
normal exit, cancellation and build cleanup must verify complete retirement before
any baseline or worker result is sealed. Missing acknowledgment is incomplete
evidence. Ordinary portable inline baseline execution remains supported.
Empty selections validate selection/tooling only and do not constitute baseline
evidence. Assess the baseline receipt and every planned worker report together.

Selected counts, completed outcomes, baseline evidence, tool exits and summary
counts must agree. A zero selection is recorded explicitly and may have no report;
a stale report is rejected. Real dependency-free fixtures exercise the pinned CLI,
caught/advisory outcomes, baseline failure, empty selection, hanging mutations
and shared-baseline rejection through
`node --test scripts/release/run-mutants.test.mjs`. Individual process watchdogs
remain distinct from the complete-suite deadline: intentional hanging-mutant
controls retain the pinned tool's caught classification, while a failed baseline
or inconclusive tool-level timeout never qualifies acceptance.

Survivors remain advisory and must be triaged in review. Unviable mutants are not
caught mutants. Timeouts, usage/diff/internal errors, absent reports and incomplete
sweeps fail the job: they are inconclusive, not successful validation. The full sweep
still has a runtime budget; a timed-out sweep is not represented as complete.
Report formats and exit codes follow [cargo-mutants documentation](https://mutants.rs/mutants-out.html)
and [the pinned exit-code definitions](https://github.com/sourcefrog/cargo-mutants/blob/v27.1.0/src/exit_code.rs).

Coverage remains a signal, not a substitute for assertions or mutation review. Do
not count test-module lines as production-only coverage, unviable mutants as killed,
or skipped/inconclusive native scenarios as passed.

## Release workflow
# Core workflow and platform evaluations

Product evaluations are separate from prompt/agent/model evaluations. A successful
build, coverage percentage, PNG file signature or mocked browser session alone is
not evidence that the shipped desktop workflow works.

## Layers and honest boundaries

The protected CI matrix runs Rust workspace unit/integration tests and frontend
Vitest unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows. Linux records Rust `llvm-cov` and
frontend V8 coverage; the frontend report includes every production `.ts` and
`.tsx` file, including files with zero unit coverage. The `src/store` line gate
is 70%. Run `cd frontend && npm run test:coverage` locally to inspect the
frontend report in `frontend/coverage/`. Browser and native E2E assertions do
not contribute to this unit coverage percentage, so low component percentages
must be read alongside the scenario matrix below.

tests serially, continuing through independent suites after a failure while

The native runner retains the 13 contact-hiding/invisible-mode scenarios and adds
registration/sign-in, logout/invalid-password recovery, signed discovery,

name: AI Eval

# Deterministic eval-smoke and harness tests run on PRs that touch prompts, agent rules,
# workflow wiring, or eval assets. The real model-backed eval is semi-automatic: configure
# AI_EVAL_COMMAND as a repository secret and run this workflow manually, or let the path

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "AGENTS.md"
      - ".claude/**"
      - "docs/evals/**"
      - "scripts/ai-eval*.mjs"
      - "scripts/ai-eval-smoke.sh"
      - "scripts/run-real-smoke.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/ai-eval.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  deterministic:
    # Every PR executes these contracts in the shared Health caller.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    name: Deterministic eval contracts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Eval smoke
        run: make eval-smoke
      - name: AI eval harness tests
        run: node --test scripts/test-ai-eval.mjs

  real-ai-eval:
    name: Real model-backed AI eval
    needs: [provider-status]
    if: needs.provider-status.outputs.configured == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      AI_EVAL_COMMAND: ${{ secrets.AI_EVAL_COMMAND }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Run real AI eval when provider is configured
        run: make ai-eval
      - name: Upload AI eval report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ai-eval-report
          path: target/ai-eval/
          if-no-files-found: error

  provider-status:
    name: Report AI provider availability (not an eval result)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      configured: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.configured }}
    steps:
      - name: Disclose whether real model evaluation can run
        id: provider
        env:
          AI_EVAL_COMMAND: ${{ secrets.AI_EVAL_COMMAND }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "${AI_EVAL_COMMAND:-}" ]; then
            echo 'configured=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'Real-model provider configured; evaluation verdict comes from the separate job.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo 'configured=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'Real-model evaluation NOT RUN: provider unavailable. Deterministic contracts are not model-backed eval evidence.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
# Protocol fuzzing

The `fuzz/` crate is outside the main Cargo workspace because its libFuzzer runner uses a
nightly toolchain. Its targets call the same public decode entry points used for untrusted
network frames and opened peer payloads. The weekly and manual [Fuzz workflow](../.github/workflows/fuzz.yml)
iterates over every target; a crash artifact is uploaded for reproduction.

The current targets cover LAN announcements, message and reaction payloads, DM and recall
envelopes, channel metadata and sender keys, ratchet state and headers, file manifests,
signed account profiles, device-pairing frames, and call-signal envelopes. The new framed
targets try both the raw input and the expected magic prefix so mutations reach the
payload parser as well as the framing check. Profile inputs also exercise signature
verification when decoding succeeds. Call signaling is experimental; this target covers
its Rust envelope decoder, not media or WebRTC behavior.

```bash
# Fast compile check; stable Rust is sufficient for this check.
cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Coverage-guided run (requires rustup nightly and cargo-fuzz).
cd fuzz
cargo +nightly fuzz list
cargo +nightly fuzz run profile_payload_decode -- -max_total_time=120
```

Fuzzing checks for panics and crashes. It does not prove that accepted payloads are
semantically valid or that the end-to-end protocol is secure. Keep deterministic decoder
assertions in the core tests and run `make e2e` for real multi-process behavior.

p=Path('docs/testing-feedback-loop.md');s=p.read_text();anchor='## Completion and retirement evidence';section='''## Foundation verification method allocation

Use the [F01 scenario map](module-boundaries.md#scenario-routes-and-available-verification)
to choose a boundary before choosing a method. The following allocation covers
REQ-003/030 without making every named technique a mandatory check. Existing
workflows and capability contracts remain authoritative; a listed tool or test
is available evidence infrastructure, not a current passing result.

| Method family | Existing owner / evidence surface | Foundation use, gap and next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Static/type/semantic analysis and SAST | Rust fmt/Clippy, frontend TypeScript/ESLint, CodeQL, structural standards. | Run affected checks locally; retain protected source/security checks. Validation owner reviews semantic caller/authority edges that static imports cannot establish. No formal proof follows from lint success. |
| Formal/model checking | Authority and lifecycle invariants in owning guides and focused regressions. | No formal-verification execution established by this inventory. Core owner may select a bounded state machine if a concrete ambiguity justifies a model; do not introduce a mandatory prover or claim exhaustive interleaving coverage. |
| Unit/integration/contract checks | Crate/frontend `validation.json`, Rust inline tests and integration targets, Vitest and script fixtures. | Default local feedback. Inspect negative/recovery assertions and nonzero executed counts. Integration filenames require explicit targets when the library fallback does not select them. |
| Browser, native and process E2E | Playwright, native desktop runner, backend CLI runner and supported-platform workflows. | Qualify real interactions at their actual seam. Browser IPC mocks do not certify native lock/session lifecycle, physical media or cross-LAN behavior. Native/platform owners retain those gaps. |
| Property/generative and fuzz checks | Deterministic `decoder_smoke` arbitrary-byte sweep; `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` and scheduled fuzz workflow. | Stable smoke is the cheap local panic boundary, fuzz explores input space separately. Neither proves accepted payload semantics. Protocol owner keeps entry-point inventories aligned and retains valid/invalid semantic tests. |
| Mutation testing | Existing mutation runner and scheduled/manual product samples. | Validation owner uses survivors to identify weak assertions. PR runner-fixture success is not product mutation coverage; inconclusive/timeout outcomes remain failures of evidence. No per-edit full mutation sweep. |
| Runtime/DAST | Real local integration transports, authenticated network tests and native acceptance. | Integration/privacy owners exercise invalid grants, malformed input and live revocation at service boundaries. No generic DAST scan or whole-service security certification is claimed; select a concrete exposed boundary first. |
| Load/stress/spike/soak/capacity | Existing bounded queue, admission, growing-history and progress regressions; performance budgets. | F03 owns reproducible workload/window measurements. A deterministic saturation test is not a sustained soak or platform capacity baseline. Add a targeted stress scenario only for an observed growth/progress risk. |
| Memory/leak/undefined behavior/races | Core ASan/LeakSanitizer workflow; held-worker and contention regressions. | Preserve the core instrumentation scope. Host/native libraries and scheduler interleavings remain separate; no TSan, Miri or exhaustive race proof is established. F03 measures real process-family memory separately. |
| Coverage: statement/branch/condition/function/path/MC/DC | Rust llvm-cov, frontend V8/LCOV, browser coverage union and existing patch checks. | Report only metrics actually emitted and their source scope. Condition, path and MC/DC completeness are not inferred from line/branch reports. Validation owner ties uncovered risk to assertions rather than a new percentage target. |
| Maintainability/review | Module contracts, source/caller review, standards and repository hygiene. | Review ownership, lifetime, error and recovery semantics. File counts, scores and a clean checker cannot replace design review. Local sequential work preserves reviewed commits; publication remains separate. |
| CVE/secrets/dependency/supply chain | cargo-deny, npm audit, Gitleaks, dependency review, CodeQL and pinned CI tooling. | Security/build owners retain existing gates and triage concrete findings. No new policy waiver or dependency installation is implied by F02. |
| Licenses/compliance | Existing license policy and dependency checks. | Dependency owners review applicable license findings. Product owner resolves an actual external compliance requirement; no unnamed regulatory certification is claimed. |
| Fault injection/degradation/recovery/chaos | Interrupted writes, held work, unavailable peers, restart/replay and source-loss fixtures. | Prefer deterministic faults at the actual commit/ownership boundary. Preserve progress after recovery and exact original effects. Broader distributed chaos requires a topology and failure hypothesis, not a blanket suite. |
| Agent tools/format/authorization/multi-turn/factuality | Integration service/MCP tests, deterministic AI-eval harness and model-backed source-review suites. | Service owner qualifies real schema/grant/destination/idempotency boundaries; evaluation owner records whether a model actually ran. | RAG/ML evaluation | No retrieval/model-training product surface established in the inspected current-IM paths. | Not applicable to this foundation slice. Revisit only when such a surface is activated; do not confuse source-review AI tooling with a shipped RAG product. |

### Reproducible local foundation checks

Reuse the managed stage reports under `target/validation/attempts` and
`target/validation/feedback`. Record source and dirty paths, selector, actual test
count, compiler duration, harness duration, queue and full process exit. Do not
subtract unrelated runs or treat a warm compile as a product speedup. Run
`make validation-report` for existing observations; missing phase timestamps stay
unknown, and one attempt cannot establish a flake rate or p95 distribution.

The first bounded authority/lifecycle checks are:

- `make test-focused TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync::personal_replay_tests`
  checks old buffered replay after cleanup acknowledgement and permits fresh
  authorized content without resurrecting the removed content.
- `make test-focused TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::participant_runtime_tests`
  checks preparation, event/deadline wakeups, held-worker retirement and rejection
  of new work after stop. It does not exercise every desktop producer.
- `make test-focused TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=prepared_member_send_recovers_exact_sidecars_and_terminal_on_node_restart`
  interrupts completion, reopens the same store and checks the original event,
  single sidecar, cleared pending journal and idempotent terminal result.
- `make test-focused TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_TARGET=decoder_smoke`
  runs the actual integration target; a `--lib` selector is insufficient.
- `cd frontend && npm test -- src/store/ownership.test.ts src/features/chat/ConversationViewIdle.test.ts src/store/accountGroupOperations.test.ts`
  checks UI ownership/operation observation and unchanged-viewport behavior. This
  does not supply desktop process CPU or native cancellation evidence.

of those boundaries, not complete F02/F04 or F10 acceptance. Broad recovery,
privacy, membership, supported-platform and runtime-budget qualification remains
owned by the scenario map.

Retain these existing seams for the initial foundation slice. The focused
[verification commands](testing-feedback-loop.md#reproducible-local-foundation-checks)
exercise their narrow failure/recovery conditions; no extraction is justified
solely by the number of modules.

  callback in current session/runtime/app-lock checks. Its `detached` owner keeps
  the runtime read guard while actual work runs. Frontend ownership checks only
  fence UI publication; they are not the durable commit authority.
- Current group text submission captures the host owner and expected account,
  then calls `submit_account_group_text_if`. The core retains the operation ID
  independently of its resulting public event. The prepared-send restart test
  checks replay of the original durable effect without another message or sidecar;
  it does not establish all announcement/member transitions.
- Personal replay captures an authorization cut for the requesting sibling.
  A later cleanup acknowledgement cannot authorize an already-buffered old page.
  The replay regression checks both rejection of removed content and progress for
  unrelated/fresh authorized content. This is not a backup-restore or deletion-floor
  compaction proof.
- Participant stop must wait for owned blocking work after its observer is
  cancelled, join the work after release and reject later work. Existing event
  tests also distinguish ordinary presence renewal from a meaningful route change.
  Native sleep/resume and all host producer composition remain separate evidence.

F03 consumes the [scenario/store inventory](module-boundaries.md#stores-and-resource-ownership).
Before a runtime measurement, bind the executable to source, target, resolved
production features, toolchain and build profile; record executable hash and
fixture identity. Core test builds intentionally enable `fast-test-kdf`, and
SQLCipher test configuration also reduces its work. Their startup timings cannot
qualify normal password derivation or shipped startup. Existing binaries without
provenance are inspection leads, not attributable production baselines.

Use task-owned synthetic profiles and explicit isolated network ports. Never
reuse an active personal profile, remove its lock or stop an unrelated running
app to manufacture a quiet baseline. Record concurrent host activity; a noisy
window cannot establish the reference idle budget. Build/test work must finish
before the observation window starts.

An empty headless source build can qualify measurement plumbing and its own idle
behavior only. It does not substitute for the reference retained-history fixture,
desktop visible/hidden process family, active messaging/catch-up or return-to-idle
acceptance. Record CPU time versus elapsed time, RSS versus private commit, and
measured disk/network versus unavailable counters explicitly. Missing energy or
wakeup observations stay unknown. Avoid calling first use of a new profile a cold
restart of retained history.

For a bounded first baseline, measure the existing CLI with a fresh profile and
production KDF, retain its actual PID and graceful `/quit`/exit evidence, then
repeat with the same fixture for warm restart. Admit the reference workload only
after the fixture producer and counters are reproducible. F03 owns those missing
inputs; no database/UI replacement or numeric target change follows from this
preliminary baseline.

## R03: Actual work owns its lifetime

Keep concurrency capacity with the same actual owner as retirement admission.
Cancelling a scheduler must not release a serial maintenance slot while its
blocking worker or captures remain alive. Acquire only at top-level local-work
entries, outside business guards; keep network waits and leaf calls independent.
The `shared_local_repair_actual_owners` regressions hold real Profile work,
require account-local queuing, verify foreground Noise progress and retain dirty
follow-up or cancel the queued owner during retirement. The RuntimeWork
`local_repair_capacity_outlives_blocking_captures_and_panic` control checks capture,
output and panic cleanup before releasing capacity.

Before reopening a profile, consume and await `NodeRuntime::stop`; dropping the
runtime requests cancellation but does not join its actual storage owners. Keep
exclusive-open failures fatal rather than retrying around a live owner. The
[cached-route restart fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_privacy_tests.rs)
awaits both original runtimes before asserting that an offline cached route is
not fresh presence; retirement's held-writer controls retain lease exclusion.
Direct Node fixtures must also close work admission, join their accept owners,
drain actual admitted children/blocking captures, and consume `close_profile`
before reopening storage. Aborting and joining only the accept-loop parent does
not certify that its children released the profile. The
[retired-metadata recovery fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/unrestricted_messages_tests.rs)
retains durable history/search/backup assertions across that exact boundary.

A UI read watchdog retires observation, not the native operation. Coalesce a
same-owner/query refresh against the original promise until settlement, retaining
one valid follow-up; reset or query replacement must not let stale work publish
or block a new intent. The [Favorites store tests](../frontend/src/store/messageFavorites.test.ts)
hold the actual list promise beyond its UI deadline before requesting refresh.
The [serial view reader tests](../frontend/src/features/chat/useSerialPoll.test.ts)
apply the same lifetime rule to recovery timers and event coalescing, including
hidden views and a follow-up admitted after all 64 read slots were occupied.

Consume the canonical process owner's result contract rather than deriving a new
## R06: Exact authority and stale completions

When projecting account roles into device-shaped display fields, derive the
representative from the current validated account membership. A historical
legacy device owner cannot describe a transferred account role. Keep exact
account/device validation and bounded-snapshot inclusion together at the
[inventory publisher](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/inventory.rs);
the real modern and legacy transfer regressions in
[owner target tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/owner_targets.rs)
check readable inventory while preserving grants and the legacy owner field.

**Failure pattern:** work authorized before an await or queue delay commits after
logout, same-user relogin, account replacement or a policy off/on transition.
Comparing only the username or current Boolean value misses changed authority.

Capture the owner's exact session/runtime installation and relevant revision at
entry. Revalidate through the existing atomic commit seam before side effects
and before publishing private results. Treat frontend generation guards as UI
ownership, not host authorization. Read commands can expose stale private data too.
When consolidating repeated database reads, keep reuse inside the current
synchronous connection owner. Preserve identity/generation error precedence and
retirement-job integrity before reading capability metadata, and repeat live
session/deadline validation at its final owner. The repository network validator's
[regressions](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/repository/network/tests.rs)
count executed scope reads and retain stale-view, corruption and capability-change
controls; a prepared-statement compilation count does not measure executed reads.
Bind session effects to exact owner/generation rather than a replaceable display
object. Cosmetic profile refreshes must not restart inactivity timers, republish
call state or count as user input. The mounted [App regressions](../frontend/src/App.test.ts)
exercise metadata updates, actual input and same-owner session replacement.

A closing popup's delayed cleanup can outlive a newer popup's focus ownership.
Default restoration may act only while focus is neutral or still belongs to the
closing content. Reuse the [shared focus owner](module-boundaries.md#dialog-focus-ownership)
for dialogs and context menus; preserve consumer cancellation and ordinary trigger
restoration. The real Radix controls hold old unmount cleanup until a newer
popover owns focus, then require that popover and its action to remain usable.

A routing or capability preview must not become a second admission owner. When
| Layer                                       | Owns                                                                                          | Depends on                                              | Must delegate                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Protocol core: `crates/mesh-talk-core`      | Identity, membership, encryption, admission, persistence, transport and delivery correctness  | Rust libraries and its internal modules                 | Native platform behavior and presentation                            |
| Desktop host: `src-tauri`                   | Session/runtime installation, OS integration, settings persistence, authorized IPC adaptation | Core public exports                                     | Wire validation, cryptographic authority and delivery state machines |
| Typed IPC: `frontend/src/lib/api`           | Command names, payload shapes, typed results                                                  | Shared types, Tauri APIs and sibling adapters           | UI stores, React features and business decisions                     |
| Application stores: `frontend/src/store`    | Reactive state, owner-scoped work, optimistic intents, cache transitions                      | Typed adapters and shared projections                   | Core authority and feature rendering                                 |
| Feature modules: `frontend/src/features`    | User interaction and composition                                                              | Stores, typed adapters, shared models and UI primitives | Reimplementation of identity, policy or delivery rules               |
| UI primitives: `frontend/src/components/ui` | Accessible visual controls                                                                    | React/Radix and styling helpers                         | Session lifecycle and protocol policy                                |

The bot integration service in `crates/mesh-talk-integrations` depends on the core
and host-supplied admission ports. It owns grants, bounded metadata audit and
private IPC and its fixed-route loopback HTTP adapter; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp` owns SDK/stdio translation only. Core
`node/outgoing_message.rs` owns retry-safe event acceptance and sender-state WAL
recovery. Desktop `src-tauri/src/integrations.rs` binds exact-session leases and
graceful listener retirement. `integrations/local_access.rs` owns serialized
settings/startup control and the single desktop service handle;
`integrations/instructions.rs` owns only the marked user-level bootstrap file.
Both transports share one integration service/registry and core sending path.
`http.rs` owns public static discovery, request limits and fixed scoped routes;
request schemas derive from the existing models. The Agent access settings UI uses
the shared save coordinator and an explicit-owner typed adapter. See
[desktop local access](bot-integrations.md#desktop-local-agent-access).

The local access owner persists absolute authorization deadlines and preserves
them across service retries and session/runtime restarts. Only an explicitly
verified enable, duration extension or renewal can extend authority. The shared
integration grant authorizer checks expiry again at core acceptance. The desktop
activity view uses the existing registry's bounded content-free send projection:
read the live service registry while its supervisor exists, and open the saved
registry only after its writer has stopped under the same controller serialization.
The UI never creates a second grant-store owner or attributes a shared credential
to a particular AI application. See [authorization lifetime](bot-integrations.md#lifecycle-and-authority).

The headless CLI uses the core directly. A protocol change should not require
Tauri; a presentation change should not alter the wire protocol. Not every helper
in `lib/` is pure: `theme.ts`, for example, owns reactive appearance effects. Use

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.
